invests.text: PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 7.1S 69.3E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 7.1S 68.9E, APPROXIMATELY 213 NM WEST OF DIEGO GARCIA. ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE IMAGERY (MSI) DEPICTS AN INCREASINGLY OBSCURED, CONSOLIDATING LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) WITH PERSISTENT CONVECTION BUILDING OVER THE LLCC. A 240255Z SSMIS F16 91 GHZ MICROWAVE IMAGE DEPICTS CURVED, DEEP CONVECTIVE BANDING SLOWLY CONSOLIDATING AROUND THE LLCC TO THE NORTH. A RECENT OBSERVATION AT 111155Z FROM DIEGO GARCIA SHOWS WINDS FROM THE NORTHWEST AT 14 KNOTS WITH AN MSLP OF 1011 MB. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A MODERATELY FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH HIGH VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF 20-25 KNOTS, STRONG RADIAL UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SST) OF 28-29

PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 7.1S 76.0E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 8.9S 78.6E, APPROXIMATELY 376 NM EAST- SOUTHEAST OF DIEGO GARCIA. THIS CANCELS REF A (WTXS21 PGTW 230330). ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE IMAGERY (MSI) DEPICTS A POORLY ORGANIZED, PARTIALLY EXPOSED LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC), WITH WEAKENING CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY WEST OF THE LLCC. THE MSI ALSO DEPICTS A HIGHLY TILTED VORTEX, WITH THE LLCC LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 120 NM EAST OF THE ASSESSED MID-LEVEL ROTATION. ADDITIONALLY, STRONG LOW-LEVEL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES ARE MOVING INTO THE REGION FROM THE NORTHWEST, WHICH WILL FURTHER DISRUPT THE LLCC. UPPER LEVEL ANALYSIS INDICATES DECENT EQUATORWARD OUTFLOW ALOFT WITH MODERATE (15-20 KTS) VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS). GLOBAL MODELS INDICATE A PERSISTENT INCREASE TO VWS AS THE SYSTEM CONTINUES THE PROJECTED FORECAST TRACK AND NO LONGER DEPICT AN INTENSIFYING SYSTEM. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1006 MB. IN VIEW OF THE UNFAVORABLE FORECAST FOR THIS SYSTEM, THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS DOWNGRADED TO LOW. SEE REF A (WTXS21 PGTW 241900) FOR FURTHER DETAILS.
